name: Hardware backed keys (Keystore and Secure Enclave)
plain: Creates cryptographic keys that never leave the phone's secure chip.
meaning: A device-bound key proves that a request comes from one specific phone. The iOS Keychain can survive app deletion, which lets services recognise a returning device.

android.prompt_ui: Key is deleted on app uninstall; user auth binding optional
android.api_surface: KeyGenParameterSpec, StrongBox (API 28), setUserAuthenticationRequired, key attestation, Play Integrity
android.note: Hardware attestation certificates prove device model and OS patch level.

ios.revocation: Delete data via Settings; erase device
ios.api_surface: Keychain Services, kSecAttrTokenIDSecureEnclave, SecAccessControl .biometryCurrentSet, App Attest
ios.note: Items without a data protection class limit survive reinstall; Secure Enclave keys are only P-256.

limits.headline: Can make secret keys that stay locked inside your phone's security chip
limits.user_action: Nothing, or you confirm with fingerprint or face when the app sets up secure sign in
can: Create a key in the phone's secure chip
Sign data or log in with that key without exposing it
Require your fingerprint or face each time the key is used
Prove which phone model and security patch level it is on (Android)
cannot: Take the key out of the chip or copy it to a server
Use the key after you remove the screen lock, when set to require one
Use other key types in the iPhone Secure Enclave; it only supports P-256
Move the key to a new phone
limits.reach_label: Keys only usable on this phone
limits.differs: Android can prove the model and patch level. iPhone Secure Enclave keys are limited to one key type and are checked by Face ID or Touch ID.

story.what_it_is: An app makes a secret key that is stored in a locked chip and never leaves your phone.

marketing.name: Android Keystore
marketing.pitch: Keys live in protected hardware so even malware cannot copy them out of the phone.

marketing.name: Secure Enclave
marketing.pitch: A separate chip that holds keys and checks Face ID or Touch ID without sharing them with the app.

story.for_you: You never see the key. What you notice is smooth, safe actions like approving a payment with a face scan, and a login that does not need a password. The secret stays on the phone.
story.for_makers: Makers can prove that a login or payment came from one specific phone, which is strong protection against stolen passwords. The key can also tie an account to a device, and on iPhone some keychain items survive an uninstall, which helps services recognize a returning phone.

use_cases.example: A bank signs each money transfer with a hardware key so a stolen password alone cannot move funds.
A wallet app approves a tap to pay with a key that only unlocks after you scan your face.
A game uses a device key to sign purchase requests and block fake receipts.
A company ties staff logins to company phones with keys, so a copied password is useless on another device.
A cryptocurrency app keeps its signing key inside the chip so malware cannot read it.
A digital car key stores a key in the chip so your phone can unlock and start the car.

story.android_note: Android may keep keys in the main secure chip or a separate StrongBox chip, depending on the phone model.
story.ios_note: iPhone keychain items can survive deleting an app, so a service may still recognise a returning phone.
